PUPPET language and camera: PUPPET v2 language. First line: film title="..." style=puppet fps=24 size=1920x1080 (add voices=off for a film with subtitles instead of recorded voices; look=warm is the default lamp light, look=none switches it off). cast <char> on <plate> at x,y size=0.62 facing=left|right mood=neutral|happy|angry|shocked as=<stage>: puts a code character on a plate; several cast lines on one plate make one stage with several people; as= names a second staging (a close-up: size=0.92 at 0.5,0.47). shot A-Bs: <set|plate|stage> + camera (push pull pan focus snap handheld dutch whip shake); shots touch. say <char|set> "line" at Xs mood=... [file=recording]: only the speaker's mouth moves, the others blink; a char must be cast on the shot's plate, a set must be the shot. voice "[deep] ..." at Xs: off screen. prop <name> at x,y size= A-Bs; prop <name> in=<char>.hand; act <char> holding <prop> A-Bs; fx <effect> A-Bs at x,y; sfx <name> at Xs gain=0.6; music file=<name> A-Bs gain=0.4; cut <wipe|iris|dissolve|whip|dip|dip_white|page|slide> at Xs (on a shot boundary); text "..." at x,y size=0.05 font=ptsans|oswald|caveat color=#fff halo=0.8 A-Bs; fade in/out A-Bs. Full body: cast <char> on <plate> at x,y body=full size=0.7 facing=right as=<stage> puts the whole puppet with its feet at x,y (y about 0.95); act <char> <move> A-Bs [to=x] makes it move: walk/run with to=x cross the stage, wave point shrug facepalm arms_crossed hands_on_hips typing holding_phone thinking sit jump fall bow dance nod head_shake laugh; between acts it breathes. Use full bodies for wide shots with action, busts for close-ups of talk. Keep full bodies at least 0.12 apart at every moment. One time range per line: fade, act and text go on lines of their own, never on the shot line. With voices=off write each line also as a subtitle: text "— line" at 0.5,0.9 size=0.05 font=ptsans color=#ffffff halo=0.8 over the same seconds. About 6 syllables a second. || PUPPET: camera parameters of shot tags: camera, push, pull, snap, pan, dutch, whip, handheld, shake, focus push=0.05   slow push in over the whole shot. 0.02 near-still, 0.04-0.06 slow, 0.1 clear, 0.14-0.16 strong. Default 0.04 if you write nothing. pull=0.25   starts close, pulls back to the whole frame. Reveals. Do not combine with push. focus=0.5,0.4   point the push moves to (x,y 0..1). Put it on the face. pan=right   slow drift; left|right|up|down. Adds a small zoom. For landscapes, maps, rows of things. snap=44.3   crash zoom at that FILM second (must lie inside the shot). Put it on the reaction or at the start of the last line. handheld=1   uneven wander, like a news or reality camera. dutch=10   tilted horizon in degrees (8-12, sign gives side). Unease, problems, lies. whip=left   the shot flies in from the side, 0.35 s. Fast cut between people or a new arrival. shake=0.003   trembling. Impact, wind, panic. Keep 0.002-0.004. Combine at most two moves per shot. Never use push above 0.3. || PUPPET: camera grammar tags: camera grammar, when to push, snap, dutch, whip, handheld, pull Serious face, absurd content: the camera behaves like real TV of that genre. push 0.04-0.06: default for a talking head. Stronger push 0.1 on the strange detail or a confession. near-still push=0.02: the straight man asking questions; contrast makes the answer funnier. snap: once or twice per film. Always on the last line or the reaction to it. Not on setup lines. pull: openings (reveal the studio), the false ending ("спасибо, что пришли"), the final pull-out of a documentary. handheld: news field reports, reality, unboxing selfie, wedding guests, taxi. Not in a studio interview. dutch: commercial "problem" beat, lies, guilt, a client in crisis. Never on two shots in a row. whip: talk-show surprise guest, game-show contestants in turn, family dinner back-and-forth. pan: landscapes, maps, museum rooms, apartment tours, the table of ingredients. shake: impacts, gavel, wind at a field report. Use at least 3 different moves in a film. Never 4 identical shots in a row. || PUPPET: camera per format tags: camera, format, map Interview F01, podcast F15, therapy F07: slow push on guest, near-still host, push on the pause, pull on the false end, snap on the turn. Talk show F02: pull from host to hall, whip on the surprise guest, snap in silence. News F03: still anchor, handheld reporter and witness, snap back to the anchor. Documentary F04, nature F13: pan the landscape, slow push, handheld whisper (F13), pull out at the end. Ad F05: dutch on the problem, snap on the product, push on the pack shot, push fast on fine print. Interview job F06, doctor F21, school F20: mostly still, slow push on the answer, snap on the decision. Court F08: still judge, push on accuser, handheld defence, whip on the witness, shake on the gavel. Cooking F09, tutorial F16, unboxing F14: pan over the table, handheld process, push on the result. Weather F10, game F11, press F12, pitch F18: pull on the opener, whip between players, handheld on the hall. Taxi F22: handheld always. Museum F23, apartment F24: pan rooms, snap on details. Toast F25: handheld, push on the groom.

PUPPET workflow, check errors, safety: PUPPET: how to work tags: workflow, order, start 1. Read the request. Pick ONE format (F01-F25) that fits; search "PUPPET format Fxx" for its beats. 2. Pick 2-3 characters (ch_ codes) and 1-2 places (pl_ codes). Use only names from the catalog. 3. Write the joke first, in Russian, as 8-12 short lines. Decide the last line before anything else. 4. Lay the lines on the format beats. One line per shot. 35-55 s total. 5. Compute times: line length = words/2 s + 0.5 s per [pause]; shot = 0.3 s lead + line + 0.4 s tail. 6. Add camera per beat (search "PUPPET camera grammar"), music only where the format needs it, fade in and out. 7. Run check (mode=check). Fix every error by its line number. Never change words to fix timing; move times. 8. If check returns LINES_TO_RECORD, stop and show the list. Do not render. 9. Render once. Do not poll status. Output only the program, 25-45 lines. Start with 3 comments: # format: F01 Интервью / # logline: ... / # why it works: ... || PUPPET: safety rules tags: safety, forbidden, brands, real people, countries, religion, stereotypes Never write, show or name: - real people: politicians, celebrities, bloggers, CEOs, any real name of a living or historical person; - real brands, apps, banks, shops, cars, social networks, AI products; invent a neutral name or say "приложение", "банк", "чатбот"; - countries, real cities, flags, national symbols; say "город", "район", "страна" if needed; - politics: presidents, parties, elections, deputies, governors; - religion: god, churches, mosques, prayers, holidays of faiths, heaven or hell as belief; - national, ethnic or gender stereotypes as the joke; do not pick an accent voice by origin; - cruelty to children or animals as a joke. Children are smarter than adults; the system is funny, not the child. If the request asks for any of these, keep the format and the joke, replace the target with an invented one, and say in one line what you changed. || PUPPET: fixing check errors tags: check, error, fix, mode=check Check answers with "line N: ...". Fix only that line, then run check again. "no set 'x' on this device" -> search the catalog; take a listed name. Never invent a set. "set x has no talking mouth" -> the set is a place; use voice "..." instead of say, or put the speaker's ch_ set on screen. "shots must touch" -> make this shot start where the previous ends; shift all later times by the same amount. "the first shot must start at 0s" -> first shot 0-...s. "say needs a start time" / "needs its time" -> add at Xs or A-Bs. "is outside the film" -> move it inside the shots or extend the last shot. "unknown voice who=" -> use one of: narrator, journalist, lady, calm, fairy, deep, ad, salmon. "unclosed quote" -> close the quote; replace inner " with «». "is not a statement" -> only film, shot, say, voice, text, prop, music, fade. "recordings do not fit" -> keep words; re-time: line at = shot start + 0.3, shot end = line end + 0.4; shift everything after. Two failed fixes in a row: rewrite that beat shorter. || PUPPET: LINES_TO_RECORD tags: LINES_TO_RECORD, recording, voice, elevenlabs, stop If check returns LINES_TO_RECORD, the program is valid but some lines have no recording yet and the device has no voice key. Do this: 1. Stop. Do not render. Do not change the program. 2. Show the person the list as a short table: line number, voice (who), text, file path. 3. Say: record these lines with your own voice service, put each file at the given path, then ask me to render. 4. When the person says the files are in place, run check again. Then render once. Do not rewrite lines to avoid recording. Do not drop lines. Do not retry check in a loop. After recording, check may report real lengths ("the recordings do not fit"). Then re-time the shots (see "PUPPET: fixing check errors") without changing a single word, so the same recordings are reused. || PUPPET: common mistakes to avoid tags: mistakes, pitfalls, review, before check Before you run check, scan the program for these: - Lines too long: more than 2 words per second of shot. Split or cut words before check, not after. - say on a place set (pl_...): places have no mouth. Use voice, or show the speaker's ch_ set. - Shot times that do not touch, or a gap after a silent beat. Each shot starts where the last ended. - at= written in shot seconds (at 0.3s in every shot). Use film seconds: shot start + 0.3. - snap= outside its own shot. snap is a film second inside the shot. - Music under the last line. Stop it 3-6 s earlier. - The same camera on every shot. Vary: still host, pushing guest, one snap at the end. - A last line that explains, moralises or asks the viewer. Cut it to the fact. - A host who jokes. The host is straight; only the situation is absurd. - Real names, brands, cities, countries, religion. Replace with invented ones. - Film shorter than 30 s or longer than 60 s. Aim for 40-50 s. - Prose around the program. Output only the program.

PUPPET dialogue timing, music, skeleton, voices: PUPPET: sets and voices tags: sets, cast, places, voices, who, ch_, pl_ A set is one camera on one character or place. Writers-room names: ch_<code> is a character set with a talking mouth (ch_dina, ch_salmon, ch_piggybank). pl_<code> is a place set without a mouth (pl_tv_studio, pl_court). ad_cream is the beauty-commercial pack shot. say needs a set with a mouth: say ch_dina "...". A pl_ set never talks; put a voice over it. Each ch_ set has its own voice; do not write who= on say unless asked. Who is on screen talks with say on THEIR set. Someone heard but not shown: voice "..." who=<voice>. Voices: narrator, journalist, lady, calm, fairy, deep, ad, salmon, odessa, gogi. voice without a tag or who= is the deep narrator. "[ad] ..." is the bright commercial voice. Never pick an accent voice (odessa, gogi) to match a character's nationality or origin. Use only set names the catalog returns. Unknown set = check error; search the catalog, do not invent. || PUPPET: dialogue timing tags: timing, words per second, at, pause, line length Speech rate: 2 words per second. Live voices are slower, so never go above 2. Line length = words / 2 seconds + 0.5 s for every [pause] tag. Tags are not words. Start each line 0.3 s after its shot begins: shot 12-16s -> say ... at 12.3s. End the shot 0.4 s after the line ends. Shot length = 0.3 + line + 0.4. Examples: 4 words = 2 s -> shot 2.7 s (use 3). 8 words = 4 s -> shot 4.7 s (use 5). 12 words = 6 s -> 6.7 s. Keep lines short: 3-8 words. Over 10 words, split into two shots. One line per shot. Two lines never overlap. A silent shot (no line) of 2-3 s before the last line is a beat, not a gap; keep it. Tags at the start of a line set delivery: [deadpan] [tired] [whispering] [sighs] [calm] [pause]. One or two tags, not more. When check reports real recording lengths, re-time with the same rule and shift every later shot; never cut words. || PUPPET: music, text, fade, props tags: music, mood, text, fade, prop, sound music mood=<wonder|dark|bright|tense|cozy|calm> tempo=<n> A-Bs. Only these six moods. Music is a range, not a bed. It ducks under speech automatically. bright 110-120: show openers, game shows, commercial jingles. wonder 70: documentary, nature. cozy 84: family, kitchen. tense 92: court, problems, panic. calm 72: interview, therapy, podcast. dark 66: horror-flavoured documentary. Stop music 3-6 s before the last line. Silence makes the last line land. text: short caps, 1-4 words, film seconds, inside one shot. Lower third at 0.5,0.85; slogan at 0.2,0.25 on the empty left of ad_cream. color=#ffffff glow=#000000 on dark; color=#c4426a glow=#ffffff on the ad. fade in 0-0.6s always. fade out over the last 0.4 s, after the last line ends. prop only with a name the catalog returns; size 0.1-0.2; one prop at a time. || PUPPET: minimal complete program tags: example, skeleton, template film title="Цель накоплений" style=puppet fps=24 size=1920x1080 shot 0-3.5s: pl_tv_studio pull=0.2 fade in 0-0.6s music mood=calm tempo=72 0-22s voice "[deep] Сегодня в студии — финансовый эксперт." at 0.3s shot 3.5-7s: ch_dina push=0.02 say ch_dina "Сколько у вас сейчас?" at 3.8s shot 7-11s: ch_piggybank push=0.05 focus=0.5,0.4 say ch_piggybank "Ничего. Это осознанный минимализм." at 7.3s shot 11-14s: ch_dina push=0.04 say ch_dina "А подушка безопасности?" at 11.3s shot 14-18.5s: ch_piggybank push=0.1 focus=0.5,0.4 say ch_piggybank "Подушка — это я. Внутри просто воздух." at 14.3s shot 18.5-22s: ch_dina pull=0.2 say ch_dina "А вы сами на что копите?" at 18.8s shot 22-25s: ch_piggybank push=0.04 focus=0.5,0.4 shot 25-27.5s: ch_piggybank push=0.02 snap=25.3 focus=0.5,0.4 say ch_piggybank "[deadpan] На молоток." at 25.3s fade out 27.1-27.5s

PUPPET jokes: PUPPET: joke structure tags: joke, humour, setup, escalation, deadpan, turn Play the genre perfectly straight. The absurd lives only in the content. No winking, no laughing, no music cue. Setup (first 5-10 s): name the absurd premise in one plain sentence. "У нас Копилка. Финансовый эксперт." Deadpan escalation (middle): each beat takes the premise one step further, said calmly as fact. The straight man (host, judge, doctor) asks normal questions; the guest answers with dignity. Rule of three: two normal items, the third one wrong. False ending: "Спасибо, что пришли" or a summary. It makes the turn a surprise. Silence: a 2-3 s silent close-up right before the last line. Turn (last 3-6 s): one short line that flips the meaning. See "PUPPET last line". Topics: work, money, technology, bureaucracy, health, family, cities, nature, AI. The system is the target, never a weak person. Write in Russian. Short words. Concrete nouns beat abstractions. || PUPPET: the last line tags: last line, turn, punchline, ending Decide it first; build the film backwards to it. 2-8 words, never over 10. Plain, concrete, said flat: start it with [deadpan] or [tired]. It sits in the last 3-6 s of the film, alone in its shot, after a 2-3 s silent shot. It never explains the joke. Nobody reacts to it after; fade out 0.4 s after it ends. It reveals a fact that reframes everything: who the guest really is, what the prize is, where the advice leads. Good: «На молоток.» «Пробовал. Там ресторан.» «Не могу. Уйду — займут.» «Человек. Вышло дешевле.» Bad: a moral, a question to the viewer, a pun, a long sentence, a line that repeats the setup. Camera: snap at its start (snap=<line at>), or a still close-up if the scene was loud. Music: already stopped. Who says it: the format's turn speaker (search "PUPPET format" for "turn"). || PUPPET: commercial break tags: commercial, ad, реклама, break, ad_cream, jingle The break line comes from the host, flat, on a strong push or snap: "Извините. Прерываемся на рекламу." It can be the last line of the film. An ad inside a film: 6-10 s, 1-2 shots, right after the break line. Product is invented, never a real brand. The product ties back to the episode's absurd premise (salmon milt cream). Voice: voice "[ad] ..." over the product set (ad_cream). 1-2 lines, 8-14 words total. Music: music mood=bright tempo=118 over the ad range only. Start it with the ad, stop it when the ad ends. Text: 1-2 slogans in caps on the empty left: at 0.2,0.25 and 0.24,0.42, color=#c4426a glow=#ffffff, from 0.2 s after the ad starts to its end. Camera: push=0.06 focus=0.6,0.5 on the product. After the ad, return to the studio or flip roles (the guest now interviews a person). F05 film: the whole film is an ad; the turn is the fine print or the slogan.
